items.content:
중국 스파이 의혹을 받는 여성과의 관계로 논란에 휩싸인 젠슨 황 엔비디아 CEO가 불륜 사실을 인정하고 가족과 직원들에게 사과했다. 엔비디아 이사회는 외국 정보기관의 접근 의혹에 대한 독립 조사에 착수했지만, 황 CEO는 계속 회사를 이끌 것이라고 밝혔다.

황 CEO는 8일(현지시간) 엔비디아 공식 홈페이지에 공개한 메시지 에서 "나는 아내에게 충실하지 못했다. 내 행동으로 아내와 아이들에게 상처를 줬다. 내가 한 일에는 어떤 변명도 있을 수 없다"라며 "진심으로 사과한다"라고 밝혔다.

이어 "가족은 평생 나에게 사랑과 지지를 보내줬지만, 나는 그들을 실망시키고 우리가 함께 만들어온 삶에 상처를 입혔다"라며 자신의 행동에 전적인 책임을 지겠다고 말했다. 직원과 이사회, 협력사, 주주들에게도 사과했다. 그는 "엔비디아를 이끄는 것은 내 인생의 특권"이라며 "엔비디아에 전념하고 여러분의 신뢰를 되찾기 위해 노력하겠다"라고 강조했다.

이번 사과는 황 CEO와 중국 정보기관 연계 의혹을 받는 여성의 관계가 외신에 보도된 직후 나왔다. 파이낸셜타임스(FT)는 지난 6일 황 CEO가 싱가포르 데이터센터 기업 메가스피드의 전 임원 앨리스 황과 연인 관계를 맺었다고 보도했다. 뉴욕타임스(NYT)는 미국 정보당국이 앨리스 황의 중국 정보기관 연계 의혹을 조사했다고 전했다. 황 CEO는 이번 사과문에서 불륜 상대의 이름을 직접 밝히지는 않았다.

앞서 엔비디아는 황 CEO와 앨리스 황의 만남에 대해 고객사 경영진과의 통상적인 업무상 접촉이라고 설명했다. 회사 측은 고객사에 민감한 영업비밀이나 미국 국가안보와 관련된 정보를 제공하지 않았다고 밝힌 바 있다.

啊？63 岁的黄仁勋原来也是个老色批。金融时报爆料称，此前传言与英伟达老板黄仁勋，有密切关系的美女间谍 Alice Huang，其实跟他是恋爱关系。

早在去年，美国政府就知道了这件事，但是一直没有采取行动，明面上该女生是英伟达的大客户。 pic.twitter.com/LYXHmk30AG

이와 함께 엔비디아 이사회는 8일 공식 성명 을 통해 황 CEO가 외국 정보기관의 표적이 됐다는 최근 보도와 관련해 독립 조사에 착수한다고 발표했다. 사외이사들로 구성된 위원회가 외부 법률 전문가의 지원을 받아 조사를 진행하며, 황 CEO도 전면 협조하기로 했다.

이사회는 현재까지 미국의 국가안보나 엔비디아의 기업 비밀이 침해됐다고 판단할 근거는 없다고 밝혔다. 황 CEO와 경영진에 대한 신뢰도 유지한다고 덧붙였다.

황 CEO의 거취에 대해서도 엔비디아는 기존 경영 체제를 유지하겠다는 입장을 밝혔다. 악시오스에 따르면, 존 리조 엔비디아 공공정책 커뮤니케이션 책임자는 "이번 일로 엔비디아의 사업이 지체되지는 않을 것"이라며 "젠슨은 중단 없이 CEO로서 회사를 계속 이끌 것"이라고 말했다.

불륜 인정과 별개로, 앨리스 황의 중국 정보기관 연계 의혹이나 엔비디아 기밀 유출 여부는 공식적으로 확인되지 않았다. 중국 정부도 관련 첩보 활동 의혹을 부인하고 있다. 엔비디아는 황 CEO의 직무를 유지한 채 독립 조사를 진행할 예정이다.

items.title: GSMA MWC26 도하 개막, 글로벌 산업 표준 조정 및 중동•북아프리카 연결성 격차 해소 촉구
items.summary: [지디넷코리아] 통신사업자와 기술 리더, 정책 입안자, 혁신가들이 오늘 도하에 모여 3일간 전시와 협력, 토론을 통해 중동•북아프리카 연결성의 미래 모색 도하, 카타르, 2026년 11월 8일 /PRNewswire/ -- 카타르 통신정보기술부(Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, MCIT)와 협력해 개최하는 MWC26 도하(MWC26 Doha)가 8일 도하 전시컨벤션센터(DECC)에서 개막했다. 이번 행사에는 연결성 생태계 관계자들이 한
items.content:
글로벌뉴스 입력 :2026/11/09 06:10

통신사업자와 기술 리더, 정책 입안자, 혁신가들이 오늘 도하에 모여 3일간 전시와 협력, 토론을 통해 중동•북아프리카 연결성의 미래 모색

도하, 카타르 , 2026년 11월 8일 /PRNewswire/ -- 카타르 통신정보기술부(Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, MCIT)와 협력해 개최하는 MWC26 도하(MWC26 Doha) 가 8일 도하 전시컨벤션센터(DECC)에서 개막했다. 이번 행사에는 연결성 생태계 관계자들이 한자리에 모여 2030년까지 중동•북아프리카 경제에 4700억 달러 를 기여할 것으로 전망되는 모바일 경제의 다음 성장 단계를 모색한다.

MWC26 도하는 이날 셰이크 사우드 빈 압둘라흐만 빈 하산 빈 알리 알사니(Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman bin Hassan bin Ali Al Thani) 카타르 부총리 겸 국방담당 국무장관이 참석한 가운데 공식 개막했다 . 모하메드 빈 알리 알 마나이(Mohammed bin Ali Al Mannai) 카타르 통신정보기술부 장관이 환영사를 했다.

모하메드 빈 알리 알 마나이 통신정보기술부 장관은 개회사 에서 "제2회 MWC 도하는 통신 인프라에 요구되는 역량이 근본적으로 변화하는 시점에 개최된다. 인공지능이 지능형 에이전트를 통해 작업을 수행하는 방향으로 발전하면서 복원력이 더욱 뛰어난 네트워크와 첨단 컴퓨팅 역량의 필요성이 계속 커지고 있다. 동시에 글로벌 과제들은 연결 경로 다변화와 서비스 연속성 확보의 중요성을 부각하고 있다" 고 말했다.

GSMA의 비벡 바드리나트(Vivek Badrinath) 사무총장과 ITU의 도린 보그단-마틴(Doreen Bogdan-Martin) 사무총장이 무대에 올라 대담을 나눴다. 바드리나트 사무총장은 이 지역의 연결된 미래를 만들어갈 핵심 우선 과제로, 시장 간 네트워크와 서비스의 상호운용성을 유지하는 글로벌 표준에 대한 지속적인 지지와 중동•북아프리카에서 여전히 인터넷에 접속하지 못하는 사람들에게 연결성을 확대하기 위한 노력 강화를 제시했다.

GSMA의 비벡 바드리나트 사무총장 은 "발전은 모든 사람이 그 혜택을 함께 누릴 때만 의미가 있다. 이를 위해서는 2가지가 필요하다. 국경을 넘어 네트워크와 서비스, 기기가 원활하게 작동하도록 하는 글로벌 표준과 여전히 인터넷에 접속하지 못하는 사람들을 연결하기 위한 공동의 노력이다. 앞으로 3일간 ITU의 전권회의(Plenipotentiary Conference, PP-26)와 나란히 개최되는 MWC 도하에는 이러한 표준을 정립하고 네트워크를 구축하는 정책 입안자, 혁신가, 업계 리더들이 모여 이 비전을 실현하는 데 힘을 보탤 것이다. ITU의 전권회의가 이어지는 가운데, 두 행사의 동시 개최를 통해 더욱 활발해진 대화가 현재 진행 중인 중요한 논의에 기여할 것으로 확신한다" 고 말했다.

items.title: Nvidia will investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with possible Chinese spy
items.summary: In a memo to the company, Huang admitted that he had an affair.
items.content:
Nvidia’s board of directors announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation .

Nvidia also published a message that Huang sent to the company admitting that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed (though he didn’t mention her by name). A memo circulating among U.S. policymakers earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO.

“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Jensen Huang wrote. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Huang added that he’d “fallen short” of his responsibility to the company.

“To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” he said.

As the AI race between the United States and China heats up , chips, especially Nvidia’s chips, have been a major focus . Huang also seems to have a close relationship with President Donald Trump , who’s been a cheerleader of the AI ( or “superintelligence” ) industry.

In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said that it has “no reason to believe” that either national security or company secrets were compromised. It also said that Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it,” and that the board has “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.”

The investigation will be conducted by independent directors working with outside legal counsel.

In response to earlier reports about the CEO’s relationship with Alice Huang, Nvidia had said that the pair’s interactions were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with customers.

Other companies involved in the AI boom have warned employees to be wary of possible spies , including those offering sex or romance.

items.title: Nvidia is investigating Jensen Huang’s relationship with a Chinese spy
items.summary: Nvidia has announced that it is opening an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang and his relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who was reportedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on the company. A statement posted by the board of directors reads:
items.content:
Following reports that Nvidia’s CEO had a ‘close relationship’ with an AI exec the company is opening an investigation.

Nvidia has announced that it is opening an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang and his relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who was reportedly recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on the company . A statement posted by the board of directors reads:

The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.

The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.

The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.

The New York Times reported last month that Huang had developed a “ close relationship ” with the Megaspeed executive, which he later admitted was romantic in nature in a memo to the company. US officials believe she was feeding information directly back to Beijing.

Megaspeed is a customer of Nvidia and is the subject of a Commerce Department investigation into whether it was smuggling AI chips to China. The company’s AI chips are viewed as crucial to the US maintaining technological supremacy. Both the Biden and Trump administrations have restricted their sale to China. President Trump has loosened those restrictions but still bars sales of Nvidia’s most powerful chips to Chinese firms, and the Commerce Department must approve individual firms to handle the chips.

Just as importantly, Jensen Huang has gotten quite cozy with Donald Trump , and there is concern about what insights into the administration’s deliberations around AI he may have been privy to. And whether any of that information may have been shared with Alice Huang, and eventually found its way to Beijing.

items.title: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic
items.summary: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI's Dots or Meta's Muse. While Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly sho
items.content:
Future versions of Siri will be able to control third-party apps and perform more complex tasks.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI’s Dots or Meta’s Muse. While Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, the company has no illusions that it’s keeping pace with its rivals.

Two significant improvements are expected to be made to Siri in the coming months. One will give the assistant fine-grained control over Apple’s first-party apps, allowing it to do things like rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs. Those capabilities are expected to land with iOS 27.3. The bigger change, integration with third-party apps, is likely to land later, in the Spring, according to Gurman. That would let Siri place an order through Grubhub or book a dinner reservation through OpenTable, for example.

But that’s just the start. Apple is expected to push Siri to become more agentic and enable features that will allow it to perform ongoing tasks, not just one-offs. Gurman says:

Dots, Muse and Grok can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step. Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I’m told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year — not that it has much of a choice, given current consumer and market demands.

items.title: Goldman Sachs is pulling Claude Code from its bankers and traders
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.thestateofai.com/news/goldman-sachs-claude-code-traders-bankers Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50415628 Points: 499 # Comments: 309
items.content:
Goldman Sachs has restricted Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub to its engineers, cutting off traders and bankers who used the tools to track client flows and build market models. The bank barred its Hong Kong bankers from Claude in April and is now a lead underwriter on Anthropic's IPO.

Most traders and bankers at Goldman Sachs can no longer use AI coding tools at work. Internal guidance updated in October restricts Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub to the bank's engineers, Bloomberg News reported , following a review of productivity and risk concerns.

Strats, who work across trading, quantitative research and software engineering, still have access, according to a second person familiar with the matter.

The change has frustrated some traders, a person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. They had been using the tools to monitor client trading flows, model market moves and positions, and put together written and graphic material. Goldman spokesperson Nick Carcaterra said the bank makes certain AI tools available to staff "to determine the best use cases" across the firm.

As recently as July, chief information officer Marco Argenti was talking up "vibe coding" by Goldman's non-technical employees. He told Bloomberg that traders and bankers had built tools with AI and passed them to the firm's engineers, of whom there are about 12,000, to be improved.

That arrangement let the people closest to a problem build a first version without waiting for engineering time. It also meant thousands of employees without engineering training were running software that writes and executes code, on the same machines they use to handle client information.

At a conference in Turin last month, Argenti described Goldman's AI adoption in waves and said developers, more than 12,000 of the bank's roughly 47,000 staff, had made up the first. The October guidance limits the coding agents to that group.

In April, Goldman removed Claude from its internal AI platform for bankers in Hong Kong. The Financial Times reported that the bank had read its contract with Anthropic strictly , and an Anthropic spokesperson said Claude had never been officially supported in Hong Kong. ChatGPT and Gemini remained available there. JPMorgan removed Claude from its Hong Kong approved list in June.

The Hong Kong restriction was based on location and contract terms, and the new one is based on role. Goldman's in-house AI assistant, which uses models from several companies, is still available across the firm. The restriction applies to third-party agents that can write and run code by themselves.

Earlier this year, Goldman said Anthropic engineers had spent six months at the bank helping build Claude-based agents for trade accounting and client onboarding . Those agents sit in the back office and are run by Goldman's engineering teams.

Goldman and Morgan Stanley are also the lead underwriters on Anthropic's IPO , according to the S-1 filed October 26. Anthropic is expected to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT before the end of November, as we reported last week . Over the next few weeks, Goldman's bankers will be marketing shares in a company whose coding agent most of them are no longer allowed to use.

Claude Code reads files, writes programs and runs them, typically with the same access as the person using it. Code an engineer writes with it usually goes through review, testing and deployment controls before it reaches anything important. A script a trader builds to watch client flows can end up in daily use without going through any of those.

Banks are also required to keep information barriers between groups, for example between bankers working on deals and traders who could profit from knowing about them. Goldman built its internal AI platform around controls like these. A tool a trader puts together with an agent wasn't designed with them in mind, and engineers can only check it if someone sends it their way.

There is also the matter of whether anyone understands the code. Last month a Meta engineer said he now ships code he can't fully account for , and writing software is his job. A trader using an agent to model positions is less likely to know how that code handles unusual cases, which on a trading desk can mean losses.

Cost may also have played a part. Agent usage is billed by the token, and several companies that gave agents to everyone have seen spending climb. Amazon shut down an internal leaderboard after employees ran agents on pointless tasks to move up it, and Accenture now funds $29 a month of Claude per employee . Bloomberg's sources said productivity was part of Goldman's review.

Barclays said in October that it expects half its developers to be using Claude Code by the end of the year, and three weeks later named developers among 5,000 job cuts . Like Goldman, it is giving coding agents to engineers. Unlike Goldman, it is also using them to reduce how many engineers it employs.

Banks have tightened agent access in other places this fall. JPMorgan and Schwab are blocking outside agents from customer accounts , and Goldman has now set limits on which of its own employees can use them.

At State of AI, we think Goldman was right to restrict the tools and wrong in how it went about it.

A trading floor is a bad place for unreviewed code written by people who can't read it, and the information barrier problem would be reason enough on its own. Requiring that agent-written code come from people trained to review it is a sensible rule for a regulated business.

Goldman's own CIO was promoting traders' AI-built tools in July, though. Withdrawing access through a guideline update, with no replacement mentioned in Bloomberg's reporting, tells the traders who found good uses that they were the risk. Their complaints point to work the engineering team could take on, and Goldman would get more out of collecting them than out of waiting for them to fade.

items.title: He arrested a hacker, then spent 18 months clearing his own name. Now he’s a cybersecurity VC.
items.summary: Stephen Ward, a former Secret Service agent and Home Depot CISO, is preparing a second fund of roughly $250 million for Brightmind Partners.
items.content:
Every time venture capitalists write a check, they’re secretly running numbers in their heads about different exit scenarios. It’s their job as fiduciaries. But nearly all will tell you (publicly, anyway) that every portfolio company is headed for an IPO.

Stephen Ward, the co-founder of Brightmind Partners , a two-year-old cybersecurity fund in New York, says otherwise outright. “You have to sell on the way up,” he says.

Ward’s unvarnished pragmatism is one reason he stands out. Another is the size of his firm’s debut fund late last year: a whopping $250 million fund, which he closed with co-founder Gur Talpaz. A third reason is his résumé, which includes a stint with the Coast Guard, nine years in the Secret Service, and CISO jobs at TIAA and Home Depot before he ever thought about investing.

One proof point that suggests the combination is working is SGNL, the identity security startup CrowdStrike agreed in January to buy for $740 million, 11 months after Brightmind led its Series A .

Now Ward is raising a second fund, targeting roughly the same size as the first one. This time, though, he’ll be doing it without Talpaz, who left in April along with another early colleague, leaving Ward as the firm’s sole general partner. He’s betting on himself at a moment when early-stage cybersecurity startups are raising more money than later-stage rivals for the first time in more than a decade.

His unemotional approach to exits traces back to an unlikely career. Ward says he grew up in northwest New Jersey between two farms, in a family that couldn’t afford college for his older brothers. After high school, he joined the Coast Guard, inspired by a commercial of a man jumping out of a helicopter, though he says he barely knew how to swim at the time. He spent four years in search and rescue.

Afterward, he studied criminal justice at Seton Hall in New Jersey and thought half-heartedly about law school. “I didn’t know what I wanted to do,” Ward told me last week over Zoom, wearing a pale hooded sweatshirt and looking more like a basketball coach than a venture capitalist. “I was kind of lost. I missed the military and the camaraderie and all of that.”

After graduating in 1998, he says, he mailed out some 300 résumés but no one responded. A Seton Hall professor who was also a chaplain to Secret Service personnel, as well as to members of the FBI and CIA, began introducing him around, and the Secret Service called first.

The Secret Service has two primary missions: protecting people and investigating financial crimes. Ward gravitated to investigations, then to “cyber” after the September 11 attacks in 2001. That year, he married a former college classmate, an American-born Syrian Muslim. Colleagues warned him the background check would be “miserable.” (They’re still happily married.)

What came next took Ward’s life down an unexpected path. Stationed in New York, he arrested a hacker who’d pulled off the largest credit card data theft of that era. Instead of charging him, however, Ward flipped him, turning him into an informant and running him for about three years. But the hacker kept hacking behind Ward’s back, and after he was caught again, he told the agency, as a diversionary tactic, that Ward was in on it.

By that time, Ward had left for the private sector, and he ultimately spent roughly 18 months clearing his name. “It was hard to get out of bed,” he said of that period, describing the investigation as “almost like a spouse cheating on you,” given his love of the agency. The hacker ultimately received a 20-year sentence, and Audible bought the rights to the story, turning it into an eight-episode podcast called “ Operation Firewall .”

Ward’s corporate career has been a success by most measures, though he describes it as a series of jumps he really wasn’t qualified to make. His first private-sector job at J.P. Morgan, where he was recruited in 2007 to build a cybersecurity unit, was the hardest transition of his career, he says. He felt like “the dumbest person in the room,” missed his Secret Service crew, and twice thought about going back, unaware he was still under investigation. He stuck it out and now calls the investment bank the “best management school.”

Six years as CISO at the financial services company TIAA followed, and then two years at Home Depot starting in 2019. But in 2021, feeling burned out, he quit without anything lined up for the first time since age 16.

That chapter didn’t last long. The founders of Wiz, whose security software Ward had used at Home Depot, put him on a short list for a job at their company. Jeff Horing, a venture capitalist at Insight Partners, which had co-led Wiz’s $100 million Series A round in late 2020, interviewed Ward for the role, then offered him one at Insight instead.

It’s a good-news, bad-news story, given that Wiz was acquired last year by Google for $32 billion. When I asked him about it last week, Ward observed that the friend who took the Wiz job “made life-changing money,” but said it doesn’t bother him.

Regardless, he spent just three years at Insight, where he says he worked on Wiz, Abnormal Security, and Elisity, which IonQ agreed in October to buy for up to $1.3 billion. Then, at age 49, he thought about striking out on his own for the first time.

He says people told him it was a young man’s game. He left anyway and began cold-emailing limited partners. Ultimately, fewer than 20 LPs filled the fund, including Horing.

Ward started Brightmind in 2024 with Talpaz, a CrowdStrike corporate development executive whose deals overlapped with Ward’s during his time at Insight. Tayler Sipperly, another CrowdStrike corporate development alum, was the firm’s third employee.

items.title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno
items.summary: Suno is facing yet another pair of lawsuits. A group of rights holders of Elvis Presley's music and the publisher of some of Eminem's biggest records are suing the AI music company, claiming it illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The lawyers in the Pres
items.content:
Suno is facing two more lawsuits over AI music clones.

Suno is facing yet another pair of lawsuits . A group of rights holders of Elvis Presley’s music and the publisher of some of Eminem‘s biggest records are suing the AI music company, claiming it illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The lawyers in the Presley suit claim that Suno has violated Tennessee’s Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security (ELVIS) Act, which makes it illegal for an AI company to clone a singer’s voice.

In the suit, lawyers representing Presley’s rights holders argue that “Suno has mechanically encoded itself with artists’ identities, hard-work, creativity, and time, and harnessed them all for a consistent conveyor belt of cold hard cash.“ These suits closely mirror one filed by Jason Isbell and others in September, which claimed Suno created imitations of the plaintiffs but did not claim copyright infringement directly.

Later in the complaint , the lawyers write that “Suno’s ravenous race to the bottom aims to make human creativity obsolete, coldly replicating without a license in seconds what takes years to learn, struggle with, maintain, and endlessly attempt to make better and perfect.”

Suno spokesperson Cat McCormack told The Verge that, “Suno exists to help people create new, original music, not to trade on anyone’s name or likeness, and we prohibit any unauthorized use of an artist’s work. To protect against this, we do not allow prompts for specific artists’ names and songs and work with third-party providers to screen uploaded audio files and lyrics for potential misuse. We are always working to strengthen our guardrails and we will continue to add new safeguards that protect artists and our users.”

This adds to the pile of lawsuits Suno is currently facing from Sony, UMG , Isbell, Reservoir Media , and more.

items.title: TechCrunch Mobility: The Cybertruck experiment is over
items.summary: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it.
items.content:
Almost seven years ago, while clutching a laptop, my phone, and a notebook in a sea of Tesla fans, I watched head designer Franz von Holzhausen throw a metal, baseball-sized ball at the driver’s-side window of the Cybertruck . The result was cracked glass — actually, two by the end of the presentation — and some awkward jokes and chuckling by CEO Elon Musk .

I have witnessed a number of stunning, odd, and fantastical moments at Tesla events. But the Cybertruck reveal was the most interesting — and not because of the postapocalyptic design. It was the crowd.

When the truck rolled out onto the stage, I watched attendees gasp, some in revulsion. There was mumbling (“This certainly can’t be the Cybertruck ?” I heard Tesla superfans whisper). And yes, there were cheers. The momentary shock of Musk’s biggest fans was quickly replaced by support, acceptance, and finally, endorsement.

It moved like a wave over the crowd. By the time attendees were waiting in line for Cybertruck rides, the mood had shifted. Everyone was a fan.

That fandom carried over to Cybertruck reservations, which skyrocketed to 1 million, Musk said during a third-quarter earnings call in 2023. But it never made the leap to actual sales. Industry experts estimate about 71,000 Cybertrucks have been sold since the first deliveries began in November 2023.

And now the Cybertruck is headed to the scrap pile. Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck next year, Musk said Friday.

Was the vehicle too edgy? Maybe, but this was always going to be a niche market. I believe more practical reasons dampened sales. Musk promised the Cybertruck would have a 500-mile range and a price tag under $40,000. It achieved neither, senior reporter Sean O’Kane noted in his report .

Zipline has had quite the week. Strike that — quite the year. The autonomous drone delivery startup, which was founded in 2014, has steadily scaled over the past few years. But 2026 has taken the company to new heights.

In early 2026, Zipline raised $600 million and quickly added another $200 million to that Series H round. The company planned to use these funds to accelerate its expansion to at least four U.S. cities in 2026.

Now it has even more money to grow even faster. Zipline announced this week it raised $1.5 billion and ramped up its partnership with Walmart to add 300 drone delivery sites across the United States. Zipline is now valued at $21.5 billion.

Other deals that got my attention …

Electric truck startup Harbinger raised a $240 million Series D funding round as it expands its portfolio of products, including battery storage and defense applications. No word on the company’s valuation.

Humble Robotics raised $51 million in a Series A round, bringing total funding to $75 million less than a year after founding. The round was led by Obvious Ventures with participation from insiders Eclipse, Energy Impact Partners, and others.

Static Media acquired automotive news site CarScoops, adding to its existing portfolio that includes 34 brands such as Engadget, Jalopnik, and SlashGear.

Also , the micromobility startup spun out of Rivian in 2025, quietly started and then walked away from an electric two-wheeler pilot project in Kenya earlier this year, as it sought to focus its resources on its consumer e-bike and autonomous vehicle ambitions.

Amazon has made Uber Eats its official restaurant delivery partner for Prime members in the United States, effectively ending the e-commerce giant’s existing deal with Grubhub.

The Luce, Ferrari ’s first electric car and one of its most polarizing models, is “fully allocated” for 2027.

Ford unveiled what it’s calling a “privacy promise” — an “explicit commitment” to keep customers’ vehicle data safe and give them control over what they share. Ford also launched a website designed to educate customers about how, where, and why the automaker uses their data, and to show them how to change those settings.

May Mobility and Forterra advanced to phase three of the Department of Defense’s Robotic Operations for Autonomous Delivery and Sustainment (ROADS) prize challenge, an initiative to test and adopt commercial self-driving vehicles in the military.

Serve Robotics announced plans to launch a new business line called Physical AI Services. The company will still operate and expand its autonomous delivery operations and become a technology supplier to other companies building robots.

The predictions of AI agents booking restaurants, trips, and even rides for the masses hasn’t quite materialized yet. Uber reported during its third-quarter earnings call that only four rides were ordered through an AI agent during its busiest week in October: the week of Halloween.

Waymo is shaking up its Uber relationship, confirming months of speculation. The company will end its exclusivity with Uber in the Austin and Atlanta markets starting in January 2028.

We have co-bylined dozens of articles on company earnings and breaking news and co-hosted Equity, TechCrunch’s flagship podcast about the business of startups. And so it’s bittersweet to see him head off on a new adventure at the Wall Street Journal to cover Tesla.

Congrats on the gig, Sean! We hate to see you go!

I will, of course, continue to deliver readers insider details, scoops, and analysis about the future of transportation, from autonomous vehicle technology and EVs to automotive tech and the future of flight.

Got a tip for me? Email me at [email protected] .

items.title: Apple’s M5 MacBook Air is down to its lowest price since July
items.summary: The latest 13-inch MacBook Air is currently available for $1,099.99, marking the second time we’ve seen this $200 discount following the company’s hefty price increases over the summer. Although the base model — which features Apple’s M5 processor, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of stora
items.content:
You can get a temporary break from the $200 price hike that hit both Air sizes this summer.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The latest 13-inch MacBook Air is currently available for $1,099.99, marking the second time we’ve seen this $200 discount following the company’s hefty price increases over the summer . Although the base model — which features Apple’s M5 processor, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage — often sold for around $950 to $1,000 shortly after it launched in May, savings have been rare since July, making the current deal worth flagging. Amazon , Best Buy , and B&H Photo are all honoring the price across all color options.

If you’d prefer something with a larger screen, a six-speaker array instead of four, and slightly more power (with two additional GPU cores in the M5), Apple’s 15-inch MacBook Air is also on sale for $200 off. Amazon , Best Buy , and B&H Photo are each selling the 16GB RAM / 512GB SSD configuration in most colors for $1,299.99.

Although it’s pricier than the newer MacBook Neo, the Air offers better value in numerous ways. It’s an ideal choice if you want faster performance, as it offers double the RAM and a speedier CPU with more cores. You also get twice as much storage, better speakers, a backlit keyboard, and a larger, higher-resolution screen. Given said differences, it’s easy to see how the Air’s improvements might make it worth the extra cost for some people.

If you’re still on the fence, though, I’d recommend reading my colleague Antonio G. Di Benedetto’s reviews, both of which were published before the summer price increases.

items.content:
'삼성 상대 첫번째 소송' 쟁점특허 6건 모두 재심사 청구

반도체ㆍ디스플레이 입력 :2026/11/09 00:53 수정: 2026/11/09 07:01

특허관리전문기업(NPE) 네오레이어(NeoLayer)가 삼성전자를 상대로 제기한 첫 번째 특허소송에 사용한 특허 6건 모두에 대해 삼성디스플레이가 미국 특허청에 결정계 재심사를 청구했다. 6건 중 4건은 재심사 명령이 나왔고, 나머지 2건은 특허청의 재심사 개시 결정 여부를 기다리고 있다.

9일 업계에 따르면 삼성디스플레이는 지난달 30일 네오레이어의 미국 특허 1건(7,649,583·액정표시장치, 아래 '583 특허)을 상대로 미국 특허청에 결정계 재심사(EPR)를 청구했다. 결정계 재심사는 특허성(신규성·진보성)을 문제 삼는 절차다.

삼성디스플레이는 2026년 8월부터 10월 초순까지 네오레이어 특허 5건을 상대로 결정계 재심사를 청구한 바 있다. 이번에 재심사를 청구한 '583 특허까지 더하면 삼성디스플레이가 재심사를 청구한 네오레이어 특허는 모두 6건이다.

해당 특허 6건은 네오레이어가 2025년 12월 삼성전자를 상대로 제기한 첫 번째 특허침해소송에 사용한 특허 6건과 같다. 네오레이어가 2026년 6월 삼성전자를 상대로 시작한 두 번째 소송에 사용한 특허 3건에 대해선 삼성디스플레이가 아직 특허청 재심사나 특허심판원(PTAB) 무효심판(IPR)을 청구하진 않았다.

네오레이어는 삼성전자 외에 에이수스, BOE 등을 상대로도 특허침해소송을 제기했다. 네오레이어가 2025년 12월 에이수스를 상대로 제기한 소송에 사용한 특허 6건은 삼성전자 상대 첫 번째 소송에 사용한 특허 6건과 같다.

네오레이어는 2026년 6월 BOE를 상대로 소송을 제기하면서 BOE가 특허 10건을 무단 사용했다고 주장했다. 해당 특허 10건에는 네오레이어가 삼성전자를 상대로 제기한 소송 2건에 사용한 특허 9건 중 8건이 포함된다.

삼성디스플레이가 청구한 재심사 결과는 삼성디스플레이의 또 다른 고객 에이수스, 경쟁사 BOE의 네오레이어 상대 소송에도 영향을 미칠 수 있다. 네오레이어는 2025년 7월 대만 AUO에서 특허 101건을 매입했 다. 당시 사들인 특허를 삼성전자 등을 상대로 한 소송에 사용하고 있다.

네오레이어가 특허를 침해했다고 지목한 제품은 삼성전자 갤럭시S24 시리즈, 에이수스 스마트폰(ROG Phone 9), 노트북(Q423S) 등이다. BOE에 대해선 애플 아이폰16e, 구글 픽셀9프로, 애플 맥북 에어, 하이센스 TV(32A45K) 등에 납품한 패널이 특허를 침해했다고 주장하고 있다. 아이폰16e와 픽셀9프로는 OLED 제품, 맥북 에어와 하이센스 TV는 액정표시장치(LCD) 제품이다.

items.title: Chatbots might be coming to Apple’s HomeView
items.summary: Code in the iOS 27.3 beta suggests that Apple could add support for chatbots to its smart home hub. There's a flag listed for a "Conversational Apps" category. While there are no details about what apps would fall under that heading, it seems reasonable that AI chatbots like Chat
items.content:
Code in iOS 27.3 has a flag for ‘Conversational Apps.’

Code in the iOS 27.3 beta suggests that Apple could add support for chatbots to its smart home hub. There’s a flag listed for a “Conversational Apps” category. While there are no details about what apps would fall under that heading, it seems reasonable that AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude could be added to HomeView. According to pdfu on X, that new beta also adds support for bidirectional audio routing and session management, but says it’s “still not fully wired up.”

Apple has also added anti-spoofing protection that will require a user to authenticate themselves with an iPhone after three failed attempts. It will also have a lockout system with increasingly longer wait times, starting at one hour for the second lockout, and climbing to eight for the fourth.

Neither feature has been officially announced by Apple, and there’s no word on when they might become available.
